summary.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20% to INR247.03 crore and PAT 43% to INR58.95 crore, with growth mostly from price and mix, not volume.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was INR247.03 crore (up 20% YoY), PBT INR77.79 crore (up 41%) and PAT INR58.95 crore (up 43%). Consolidated revenue was INR269.23 crore (up 25%), PAT INR56.12 crore (up 38%). Management said volume grew only about 2-3%, with the rest from price and mix, led by higher-value export sales. Raw material and freight cost inflation, linked to the West Asia conflict, were not passed on to export OEM customers; the company said it has sent price-increase requests to US customers but has not pushed them hard as markets softened.

financial_highlights.change: Export OEM INR73.56 crore; export general INR30.24 crore
Auto OEM INR56.08 crore; replacement INR36.52 crore; footwear INR41.16 crore; furnishing INR6.08 crore; other INR3.38 crore

segments.name: Export OEM
segments.commentary: INR73.56 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR53 crore in Q1 FY26 (analyst figure), roughly 39-40% growth; export volume up about 9% per management. Gross margin did not expand on this growth due to freight and raw material costs.

segments.name: Export general
segments.commentary: INR30.24 crore in Q1 FY27; no separate growth figure given.

segments.name: Domestic auto OEM
segments.commentary: INR56.08 crore; domestic volume growth overall about 1%. Management said four-wheeler volumes from Tata are at an early stage and Mahindra business should rise in coming years.

segments.name: Replacement
segments.commentary: INR36.52 crore in Q1 FY27; no growth figure given.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR41.16 crore; management said the segment de-grew as sole prices rose sharply, muting demand.

segments.name: PU (polyurethane) plant
segments.commentary: Underutilised with no change over the last three months; competition from China is intense, no confirmed business from top brands despite sampling, and management would not give a firm recommendation for the PU plant this financial year.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to top-line growth of 10-15% per year over the next 3 years, with strong growth expected in exports and not strong growth in domestic.

Sustainable margin is guided at about 25% plus or minus 1-2%, with the Q4 FY26 margin described as an abnormally high one-time forex benefit; management asked analysts to view margin on a yearly basis.
US automotive business expected to grow substantially over the next 3 years, with Ford and Chrysler wallet share gains cited; management said growth would come from existing clients.
Freight and logistics cost increases expected to ease if the war situation improves, but management did not commit to a timeline.
Price increase for US export OEM customers under consideration; management said it would depend on how the market moves over the next two to three weeks.
capex_capacity: New line ordered for the existing Gujarat plant adds 5 lakh meters of capacity, with production targeted around February-March 2027 (end of FY27).
PVC installed capacity is 3.5 million meters per month (range 3.5-4.2 million depending on mix); utilisation is about 75-78% on current production of 2.7-2.8 million meters per month.
Capex for FY27 is around INR50 crore; a further capex of about INR250 crore over the next two years is possible if an overseas plant is finalised, and not yet confirmed.

Overseas plant location still under evaluation (Mexico, US or other NAFTA locations); management said it will go overseas first and not do both expansions at once. An India expansion is a longer-term option.
Management estimated the new line adds about INR150 crore of annual revenue at INR300 per linear meter; total could reach INR250-400 crore including the additional facility, depending on mix.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 growth of 25% was about 2% volume and the rest price, driven by a higher-value export mix; management said raw material price was not the main cause.
Export volume growth of about 9% and domestic about 1%, with total volume growth about 2.77%.
Raw material prices softened a little in Q1 but remain above their early-March 2026 levels; prices were very volatile after March.
Shipping costs roughly quadrupled, and the company did not take a price increase on export OEM business, partly offset by about a 10% natural hedge from dollar appreciation.
Management said the company received a 10% price increase in US dollar terms on some business, though it said the US market is softening again.
Competition in PU is intense from China. Footwear demand was muted because sole prices rose two to three times.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 2%; the rest came from price, mainly due to an export mix shift to higher-priced items rather than raw material pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: The Gulf war raised raw material costs and shipping costs (about 4x). The company had requested price increases from export OEM customers but put them on hold when prices fell, and has not taken an increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US OEM growth outlook and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects US business to grow substantially over three years, through wallet share gains with Ford and Chrysler and new Europe RFQs. It declined to give an order book figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company should look at annual margin, which can move 1-2% either way quarter to quarter; it aims to maintain the margin level guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is 65-66% on a 48 million meter total capacity basis (PVC 3.5-3.7 million meters per month); the new line lifts capacity to about 4-4.2 million meters per month and gives 25-30% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the PU plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The PU plant is underutilised with no change in three months. Sampling with top brands has been done but no business is confirmed, and management cannot make a strong recommendation this financial year.

risks_watch: Freight and raw material costs: shipping cost reportedly up about 4x and raw material prices volatile since March 2026; company has not taken a price increase on export OEM business, so the margin recovery depends on timing of price hikes and freight easing.
US export pricing: a price increase was requested from US customers but not pushed hard; outcome depends on market moves over the next two to three weeks, per management.
Capex and overseas plant: FY27 capex about INR50 crore; a further roughly INR250 crore over two years depends on an overseas plant location not yet finalised (Mexico, US or other NAFTA).
Volume growth: total volume only about 2.77%, domestic about 1%; footwear de-grew on sole price increases; growth guidance of 10-15% is leaning on exports.
PU plant: underutilised with no change for three months, no confirmed business from top brands, and no firm recommendation for this financial year.
Other expenses: about INR9 crore QoQ rise in Q1 FY27 from freight, travel, legal, professional and risk cover costs; management could not split recurring versus one-time amounts.
key_quotes: So, we have not taken a price increase in the export market but you also have to look at one more thing in this 10% more or less natural hedge has happened.
So, we have a headroom to expand to 25%, 30% more capacity.
So anywhere between 10% to 15% growth, we are not looking very strong growth in the domestic market. But yes, we are looking at a very strong growth in the export market.
But this present quarter's margin will be sustainable and expected to continue.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth (10-15% top-line, strong exports, margin around 25% plus or minus 1-2% on a yearly basis) but noticeably cautious and evasive on near-term pricing, the overseas plant location, the PU plant and the cost split, citing market volatility. Several answers were deferred to "after taking a final call" or left without figures, such as the order book and the INR9 crore expense breakup.
